title: Exact 217-day orbit shapes give no clear HIRES error reduction for Wolf 1061
abstract: We extend a prior Wolf 1061 velocity test with exact eccentric orbit shapes. Early HARPS fits at 217.21 days reduce squared error in 94 independent HIRES values by 4.6 and 4.9 percent. Conditional 30-day block ranges include zero. Under a Gaussian model scaled to observed scatter, the fixed-shape HIRES tests have only 25 to 27 percent power at a one-percent threshold. The updated 217.914-day period gives the same qualitative result. A separate orbit search agrees with the primary fits. A larger eccentricity bound leaves the main fits unchanged. Frozen 183.95-day curves raise later HARPS error, but a trend changes their shapes and losses. These tests do not confirm or exclude a planet. Fixed periods, circular inner nuisance terms, omitted early-fit uncertainty, shared HARPS spectra and unknown activity noise limit inference. We supply code, aggregate evidence, a figure, exact source hashes and external retrieval steps. Source records remain outside the baseline bundle.

display.caption: Frozen early eccentric orbit shapes tested in later HARPS and independent HIRES data. Ranges condition on the early fit and nuisance projection.

citations.reason: We extend the same-data transfer test to exact eccentric orbit shapes and conditional power.
